findings.description: The database username and password (including the sensitive var.password) are embedded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is stored unencrypted in the EC2 instance metadata and accessible to anyone with describe-instance-attribute permissions or console/API access to the instance metadata service.

The database password is written in cleartext to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on the instance filesystem and used to build a mysqli_connect call without TLS enforcement, meaning credentials and DB traffic can be exposed both at rest on disk and potentially in transit if SSL is not enforced by the DB connection.

findings.issue_category: reference to security group not shown (out of scope note)
findings.description: The instance attaches to aws_security_group.portal_sg, a resource not defined in this excerpt or the listed resources, meaning its network exposure cannot be verified from the provided configuration; this should be reviewed separately.
storage_encrypted is set to false, meaning the RDS database storage is not encrypted at rest, exposing sensitive catalog data to disclosure if underlying storage is compromised.

publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS instance directly to the internet and significantly increasing attack surface for a database that should only be reachable from internal application tiers.

The database password is sourced from var.password directly and applied with apply_immediately, and lifecycle ignore_changes hides subsequent password rotations from Terraform state review, increasing risk of credential exposure/drift going unnoticed.

The inline policy grants wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources (Resource: "*") to the application role, violating least privilege and allowing the application (and anything that can assume its role) to fully control S3, EC2, and RDS services including modifying security groups, exfiltrating data, or altering database configuration.

The security group rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which combined with the database being publicly accessible and having an overly permissive IAM role increases the risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.

monitoring_interval = 0 and backup_retention_period = 0 combined with publicly_accessible = true and storage_encrypted = false represent an insecure default posture for a production-grade database with no defense in depth.
